newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SIMONE HAT-TRICK FIRES MILAN TO IMPRESSIVE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SIMONE HAT-TRICK FIRES MILAN TO IMPRESSIVE WIN.

text.p: Marco Simone scored a hat-trick in only 19 minutes to lead AC Milan to an impressive 4-1 victory over Rosenborg Trondheim in the European Champions' League on Wednesday.

Milan, bidding to equal Real Madrid's 30-year-old record by winning their sixth European Cup this season, bounced back from their opening Group D defeat to Porto in Italy two weeks ago with an emphatic victory over the Norwegian champions.
Simone struck after six, 23 and 25 minutes, while Liberian Geroge Weah, the world player of the year, scored Milan's fourth after 55 minutes.
Trond Egil Soltvedt briefly gave Rosenborg some hope when he cancelled out Simone's opening goal, equalising after 15 minutes.

Porto, who beat Milan 3-2 two weeks ago, stayed top of Group D after beating IFK Gothenburg 2-1 at home with Artur Oliviera scoring after 27 and 51 minutes. Jorge Costa put through his own net for Gothenburg's only goal after 72 minutes.

Reigning European champions Juventus stayed top of Group C with a 1-0 win over Fenerbahce in Istanbul. Alen Boksic, who scored the winner against Manchester United in their opening match, was the scorer again, striking after 21 minutes.

United, favoured to reach the last eight from Group C along with Juventus, scored through Norwegian Ole Solskjaer after 20 minutes and David Beckham seven minutes later to beat outplayed Rapid Vienna 2-0 at Old Trafford.

There was a surprise in Amsterdam in Group A where Grasshopper Zurich beat 1995 European champions Ajax 1-0 thanks to a 58th minute strike from Murat Yakin, who also scored against Rangers two weeks ago.
It was Ajax's first defeat in nine matches against Swiss opposition and Grasshopper now lead Group A with maximum points.

French champions Auxerre, playing in the European Cup for the first time beat Glasgow Rangers in their Group A match in Scotland with Thomas Deniaud scoring twice with his head in the 54th and 68th minutes.
Rangers' defeat means they have now played eight Champions' League matches without a win over the past two seasons. England international Paul Gascoigne scored their only goal after 71 minutes.
In Group B Atletico Madrid won 4-1 in Poland against Widzew Lodz with Diego Simeone scoring twice, while in another Group B match Borussia Dortmund beat Steaua Bucharest 3-0 in Romania.
Simeone also scored twice when Atletico beat Steaua 4-0 in their opening match and the Spaniards now lead the group on goal difference from Borussia.
